The petitions filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor vehicles Act are clubbed together as they are arising out of the same accident and the cause of action in both the cases is one and the same.

2. The brief facts of the petitioners are as under:
It is the case of the petitioners that on 17.12.2021 at about 3.30 pm., when the petitioner in MVC No.1497/2022 was driving a Auto Rickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-41-MC-6832 along with petitioners in MVC No.1498/2022 and in MVC No.1499/2022 after completing the land work at Chennenahalli to go to his residence slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road near 3rd main road, opposite to Munegowda vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192102112/
2 Amruth Mahal Apartment, Bharathnagar, Bangalore, at that the driver of the Swift Car bearing reg.No.TN-70-AB-4070 coming from Ullala in a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life came to the extreme wrong side of the road and dashed against the said Auto Rickshaw.

After the accident, Petitioner in MVC No.1497/2022 sustained sever injuries and immediately after the accident he was taken to Anupama Hospital, Magadi Road,
Bangalore wherein after first aid treatment.

Later after some days he was admitted to Smt.Jayadevi Memorial Hospital, Magadi Main Road, Chikkagollarahatti, Bangalore for further treatment and admitted as an inpatient from 21.12.2021 to 24.12.2021 for about 4 days and underwent operation.
Petitioner spent huge amount towards medicine and other incidental charges.
At the time of accident, petitioner was working as a driver and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

After the accident, Petitioner in MVC No.1498/2022 sustained sever injuries and immediately after the accident he was taken to Anupama Hospital, Magadi Road,

Petitioner spent huge amount towards medicine and other incidental charges.

After the accident, Petitioner in MVC No.1499/2022 sustained sever injuries and immediately after the accident he was taken to Anupama Hospital, Magadi Road,
Bangalore wherein after first aid treatment.

Later after some days he was admitted to Smt.Jayadevi Memorial Hospital, Magadi Main Road, Chikkagollarahatti, Bangalore for further treatment and admitted as an inpatient from 21.12.2021 to 25.12.2021 for about 5 days and underwent operation.
Petitioner spent huge amount towards medicine and other incidental charges.
At the time of accident, petitioner was agricultural work and earning Rs.10,000/- per SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.1497 to 1499/2022 month.
The accident occurred mainly due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Swift Car bearing reg.No.TN-70-AB-4070.
The first respondent is the insurer and second respondent is the RC owner of the Swift Car bearing reg.No.TN-70-AB-4070.
Both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation as claimed by the petitioners.
The Byadarahalli police have registered a case against the driver of the Swift Car bearing reg.No.TN-70-AB-4070 in crime No.0529/2021 under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
Hence, they have prayed to allow their petition.

sentences.text: The summons in all the cases have been duly served on the respondent No.1 and 2 and have appeared before this Tribunal in all the cases and filed their respective written statement.
4. The respondent No.1 has contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

It has contended that, at the time of accident, SCCH - 26 7 MVC No.1497 to 1499/2022 the driver of the offending vehicle has not possessed the effective valid driving licence and also has not have proper and valid RC/FC and permit to use vehicle on the road.
Further contended that, the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
The respondent No.1 has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of first respondent.
As such, his liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
However, he has denied the rest of the petition averments in both the cases as false and baseless.
He has contended that the driver of the Auto Rickshaw had driven the same in rash and negligent manner.
He has also contended that the insured car was not at all involved in the alleged accident.
With these contentions he had prayed to dismiss the petition in all the cases.
The respondent No.1 has contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.1497 to 1499/2022 the case.

He has denied the nature of accident, injuries,
income of the petitioners.

He has denied that, the accident occurred only due to the rash and negligent driving of the car, the Byadarahalli police have colluded with the petitioner and registered a false case against the driver of the Car in CC No.8184/2022 under Section 279, 337 of IPC.

Further contended that, the vehicle alleged to be involved in the accident has been insured vide insurance policy No.2367/63754437/SO/000 valid from 8.5.2021 till 7.5.2022 and renewed insurance policy 2311/66666632/00/000 valid from 8.5.2022 to 7.5.2023 against any such accidents and the driver of the offending car has valid DL to driver the said car.
The compensation claimed by the petition is highly exorbitant and unreasonable.
With these contentions he had prayed to dismiss the petition in all the cases.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following issues :

No.KA-41-MC-6832 and proceeding towards Chennenahalli from his land after completing the work, when he reached near 3rd main road, opposite to Amruth Mahal apartment, Bharathnagar, Bangalore, at that time Swift Car bearing Reg. No.TN-70-AB- 4070 being driven by the driver at high speed and in rash and negligent manner came and dashed against his auto rickshaw, as a result his auto rickshaw toppled and he fell down on the ground and sustained grievous injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.
Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?
If so, from which respondent?

As already stated supra the Petitioner in MVC SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.1497 to 1499/2022 No.1497/2022 in order to prove the actionable negligence, he has got examined himself as PW-1.
He has filed affidavit for his chief examination.

I have perused Ex.P.1 to P.3, P.6 and 9.

From these documents, it is clear that the accident took place on 17.12.2021 at about 3.10 pm., and the FIR in crime SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.1497 to 1499/2022 No.0529/2021 came to be registered on 18.12.2022 at Byadarahalli police station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC against the driver of Swift Car bearing reg.No.TN-70-AB-4070.

Further the records reveal that thereafter the police conducted investigation and filed charge-sheet against the driver of Swift Car bearing reg.No.TN-70-AB-4070 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.

Ex.P.6 IMV report shows that for the vehicle bearing reg.No.TN-70-AB-4070 front wind shield glass, front bumper and number plate, front bonnet, radiator and A/c condenser, front both side head light, front left side wheel fender and left side running board damaged.

The vehicle bearing reg.No.KA- 41-MC-6832 left side body, rear left side wheel fender and rear right side body damaged and wherein it has opined that this accident was not due to any mechanical defects of above said motor vehicles.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW-1 to 3.
I have perused the entire cross-examination of PW-1 to 3 and they have denied SCCH - 26 14 MVC No.1497 to 1499/2022 that accident occurred due to the driver of Auto Rickshaw.
Therefore, the learned counsel for the Respondent No.1 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW.1 to 3 to disbelieve their version.
13. On the other hand, though the respondent No.2 has taken up several contentions and examined as RW.1 in MVC No.1497/2022, RW.2 in MVC No.1498/2022 and RW.3 in MVC No.1499/2022.

During cross examination in all the cases he has admitted that,

Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective in nature.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.1497 to 1499/2022 benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of Swift Car bearing reg.No.TN-70- AB-4070 which belong to respondent No.2.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative in all the cases.
14. ISSUE NO.2 IN MVC No.1497/2022:
PW.1 has produced notarized copy of Aadhar card at Ex.P.14.
As per this document the date of birth of PW.1 is shown as 21.06.1973 and it indicates that he was aged about 48 years as on the date of accident.
15. PW.1 has deposed that prior to the accident he was hale and healthy, working as auto rickshaw driver and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But he has not produced single piece of document to show his avocation and income.

Petitioner has deposed that, due to injury he has suffered from severe pain, he was not able to lift any article or bear weight, not able to do any work,
not able to sit, squat, walk, run, climb stairs, SCCH - 26 16 MVC No.1497 to 1499/2022 cannot use Indian toilet, movement were restricted, not able to attend any work and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and suffering.
16.
As per Ex.P.8 - wound certificate
he has sustained injury to right hand with abrasion present and right foot.
Ex.P.10 - discharge summary, wherein petitioner was diagnosised laceration right big toe with abcess and he underwent operative procedures as incision and drainage of abcess under LA.
He took treatment from 21.12.2021 to 24.12.2021 for 4 days.

Petitioner has also produced 2 medical bills and 2 advance paid receipts of Rs.35,710/- which are marked at Ex.P.11 and 12.
17.
So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, Petitioner has sought for compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in road traffic accident.
But, there is no evidences that the Petitioner is suffering from any difficulties which would affect his livelihood and day-to-day activities and earning capacity.
In the absence of medical evidence to prove SCCH - 26 17 MVC No.1497 to 1499/2022 disability, I deem it proper to award global compensation.

By considering the Munegowda vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192102112/

26. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
27. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the RC owner of the offending Swift Car.
Hence, Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The primary liability is on Respondent No.1 to pay aforesaid award amount to the petitioners respectively together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 in the 'Partly affirmative' in all the cases.

28. ISSUE NO.3 IN ALL THE CASES : In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
SCCH - 26 22 MVC No.1497 to 1499/2022 -: ORDER :-
The petitions filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, are hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner in MVC No.1497/2022 is entitled for compensation of Rs.75,000/-
(Rupees Seventy five thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

The petitioner in MVC No.1498/2022 is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,50,000/-

(Rupees one Lakh only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition Munegowda vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192102112/

After the accident, Petitioner in MVC No.1497/2022 sustained sever injuries and immediately after the accident he was taken to Anupama Hospital, Magadi Road,
Bangalore wherein after first aid treatment.
The accident occurred mainly due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Swift Car bearing reg.No.TN-70-AB-4070.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective in nature.
Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.1497 to 1499/2022 benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
But, there is no evidences that the Petitioner is suffering from any difficulties which would affect his livelihood and day-to-day activities and earning capacity.
In the absence of medical evidence to prove disability, I deem it proper to award global compensation.
By considering the nature of injuries, age of the petitioner Rs.1,00,000/- as global compensation under all the conventional heads with SCCH - 26 21 MVC No.1497 to 1499/2022 interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
opennyai_summary.decision:
27. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the RC owner of the offending Swift Car.
Hence, Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The primary liability is on Respondent No.1 to pay aforesaid award amount to the petitioners respectively together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 in the 'Partly affirmative' in all the cases.
